headline: Preservation keeps valuable things from degrading—maintenance is the price of keeping what you have
universal_truth: Entropy wins without effort; keeping what you have requires active maintenance, not passive possession
fun_facts: Ancient Egyptians preserved mummies for 3,000+ years using salt, oils, and airtight tombs
The oldest known seeds to germinate were 32,000-year-old arctic lupine preserved in permafrost
Regular car maintenance can double a vehicle's lifespan
discussion_questions: What do you have that's worth preserving?
What are you neglecting that will degrade without attention?
How do you balance acquiring new things versus maintaining what you have?

hook.script: Everything degrades. Metals rust. Relationships fade. Skills atrophy. Without active preservation, entropy wins. Keeping what you have isn't passive—it requires attention, effort, and maintenance.

cliff.script: We focus on acquiring new things more than maintaining what we have. But preservation can be more valuable than acquisition. What makes preservation important?

options.text: Preservation maintains value already captured—losing what you have costs more than failing to gain what you don't; maintenance protects investment
options.response: Yes. Losing existing value hurts more than missing potential value. A well-maintained asset continues serving you. Neglected assets degrade into liabilities.

options.text: Acquiring new things is more exciting than maintenance
options.response: True, but excitement doesn't equal value—maintenance often provides better returns...

fact1.title: Entropy Default
fact1.script: Without input, everything moves toward disorder. Buildings crumble. Relationships cool. Skills rust. Preservation requires energy input to counteract natural degradation.

fact2.title: Maintenance Economics
fact2.script: Regular maintenance is cheaper than emergency repair or replacement. A small, consistent investment prevents large, sudden costs. This applies to health, relationships, and possessions.

fact3.title: Selective Preservation
fact3.script: You can't preserve everything—attention is finite. Choose what's worth maintaining. Let go of what isn't. Strategic preservation focuses effort on what matters most.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Entropy wins without effort. Keeping what you have requires active maintenance, not passive possession. Invest in preservation.

outro.script: That's Day 235. Tomorrow, we'll explore living without using up—sustainability. Until then, identify something valuable that needs maintenance.

growTrack.title: Maintenance Audit - What Needs Attention?
growTrack.activity: What valuable things are you neglecting? A relationship, your health, a skill, a possession? What small maintenance could prevent large degradation? Schedule it. Consistent small investments protect large value.
